These injuries are ante mortem in nature.
issues: Whether the respondent should be convicted under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code with death penalty
Whether the High Court was correct in converting the conviction from Section 302 to Section 304 Part II
petitioner_arguments: The appeal by the state is against the leniency shown by the High Court and for enhancement of the sentence.

Rape is a crime against the society and the resultant violence causing the death there after can be as cruel as a deliberate act which should attract the provisions of Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code.
respondent_arguments: The High Court in turn converted the same into one under Section 304 Part II though maintained the conviction under Section 376 and did pass an order of sentence of ten years rigorous imprisonment.

There seems also no reason to think for one moment for nor is there any evidence to show that A-1 who had sexual intercourse with the deceased did anything which any reasonable person would contemplate as being likely to cause injuries which would result in the death of the deceased girl.
court_reasoning: It is difficult, however, to see how, under the Indian Penal Code, in the circumstances narrated, any charge which would fall under the definition of Section 300 IPC, thereof could be sustained.
The aforesaid accused are, therefore , guilty of the offence, punishable under Part II of Section 304 of the Indian Penal Code.

Ours is a civilised society a tooth for a tooth and an eye for an eye ought not to be the criterion; civilisation and the due process of law coupled with social order ought not to permit us to be hasty in regard to the award of capital punishment
holding: The conviction and sentence awarded by the trial court to Birabar Mania (A-5), Babaji Mania (A-6), Bhira Behera @ Baba Tanti (A-7) and Madha Tanti @ Madhabananda Parmanik (A-11) under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code is upheld.
On proof of the offence punishable under Section 304 Part II read with Section 34 IPC, the aforesaid accused persons are sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 10 years.
